topics.name: Ecosystem: food chains, trophic levels, biomagnification

questions.title: Which pollutant never breaks down?
questions.text: Which of the following is a non-biodegradable pollutant?
steps: ① Biodegradable: broken down by bacteria and fungi
② Paper, wood: plant material ⟹ biodegradable
③ Vegetable peel: biodegradable
④ DDT: a man-made chemical pesticide ⟹ not broken down
∴ DDT → (b)
questions.remember: Biodegradable = broken down by microbes (paper, wood, peels, cotton). Non-biodegradable = not broken down (DDT, plastics, glass, metal cans).
questions.trap: Picking paper because it feels 'man-made'. Paper comes from wood pulp, so microbes break it down.

questions.title: Why food chains stay short
questions.text: Which of the following limits the number of trophic levels in a food chain?
opts: Decrease in energy at higher levels
steps: ① Producers trap sunlight energy: say 1000 J
② Only about 10% passes to the next level
④ After 3 or 4 levels, too little energy is left
∴ Decrease in energy at higher levels → (c)
questions.ans: Option (c) Decrease in energy at higher levels
questions.remember: 10% law: only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level reaches the next. The rest is used for life processes or lost as heat.
questions.trap: Picking 'deficient food supply'. Food is there; the ENERGY available at each higher level shrinks.
questions.ncert: NCERT Ch 13 · Section 13.1.2 Food chains and webs
questions.tryit: If producers have 20,000 J, how much reaches the third trophic level?

questions.title: Which change does not harm the environment?
questions.text:
Given below are some of the statements regarding our environment:
(i) Change in our life-styles have resulted in greater amounts of waste material generation.
(ii) Changes in attitude have resulted in use of more disposable things.
(iii) Changes in packaging has resulted in much of our waste becoming non-biodegradable.
(iv) Organic farming.
Which amongst these is not leading to any damage of environment?
steps: ① (i) More waste ⟹ damage
② (ii) More disposable things ⟹ more waste ⟹ damage
③ (iii) Non-biodegradable packaging ⟹ damage
④ (iv) Organic farming: no chemical pesticides or fertilisers ⟹ no damage
∴ Only (iv) → (b)
questions.remember: Organic farming avoids chemical fertilisers and pesticides, so it does not pollute soil and water or cause biological magnification.
questions.trap: Picking (d) because it contains (iv). Option (d) also includes (ii), which DOES harm the environment.
questions.ncert: NCERT Ch 13 · Section 13.2 How do our activities affect the environment?
questions.tryit: Give one way to reduce non-biodegradable waste at home.
questions.tryans: Carry a cloth bag instead of taking plastic bags

questions.title: Assertion–Reason: pesticides at the top
questions.text:
Assertion (A): Highest percentage of pesticides is found in tertiary consumers in a food chain.
Reason (R): Chemicals/pesticides get accumulated progressively at each trophic level.
opts: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
steps: ① Pesticides wash into soil and water; plants absorb them
② They are non-biodegradable: not broken down, not excreted
③ Each level eats many organisms of the level below
④ So the chemicals pile up at each level: biological magnification ✓ R true
⑤ The top (tertiary consumers) has the most ✓ A true
∴ Both true, R explains A → (a)
questions.ans: Option (a) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.remember: Biological magnification: non-biodegradable chemicals (like DDT) accumulate progressively at each trophic level, so the top level (often humans) has the highest concentration.
questions.trap: Choosing (b). R is exactly WHY the top level has the most: progressive accumulation.
questions.tryit: In plants → fish → bird → humans, who has the highest DDT concentration?

questions.title: 5 J for man: how much for the plant?
questions.text:
In the following food chain, 5 J of energy is available to man. Calculate how much energy was available at the producer level. Why?
Plant → Goat → Man
steps: ① 10% law: each level gets 10% of the level below
② Man (5 J) = 10% of goat ⟹ goat = 50 J
③ Goat (50 J) = 10% of plant ⟹ plant = 500 J
④ Why: ~90% is used for life processes or lost as heat
∴ Producer (plant): 500 J
questions.ans: 500 J. By the 10% law, man (5 J) gets 10% of the goat's energy, so the goat had 50 J; the goat got 10% of the plant's, so the plant had 500 J. About 90% at each level is used for life processes or lost as heat.
questions.remember: Going UP the chain: divide by 10. Going DOWN (back to producers): multiply by 10.
questions.trap: Dividing instead of multiplying, and getting 0.05 J for the plant. Producers always have the MOST energy.
questions.tryit: If a snake gets 2 J in grass → grasshopper → frog → snake, how much did the grass have?

questions.title: Decomposers: nature's cleaners
questions.text: What are decomposers? List two important roles they play in the environment.
steps: ① Decomposers: microorganisms like bacteria and fungi
② They break down complex organic matter of dead plants and animals into simple inorganic substances
③ Role 1: clean the environment of dead remains and wastes
④ Role 2: return nutrients to the soil, to be used by plants again
∴ Bacteria, fungi · clean up · recycle nutrients
questions.ans: Decomposers are microorganisms (bacteria and fungi) that break down the complex organic substances of dead plants, animals and wastes into simple inorganic substances. Roles: (1) they clean the environment of dead remains; (2) they return nutrients to the soil for plants to use again.
questions.remember: Decomposers break down COMPLEX ORGANIC matter into SIMPLE INORGANIC substances, recycling nutrients. Without them, dead matter would pile up and nutrients would run out.
questions.trap: Saying they turn inorganic into organic. That's what producers (plants) do.
questions.tryit: What would happen if all decomposers disappeared?
questions.tryans: Dead matter would pile up and nutrients would not return to the soil

questions.title: CFCs, the ozone layer and the 1987 agreement
questions.text:
(i) Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) have been linked to depletion of the ozone layer. In 1987, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) succeeded in making an agreement. State this agreement.
(ii) What is the role of ozone in our atmosphere?
steps: ① UV acts on O₂: O₂ → O + O
② O + O₂ → O₃ (ozone)
③ CFCs (refrigerants, fire extinguishers) destroy ozone
④ (i) UNEP 1987: freeze CFC production at 1986 levels
⑤ (ii) Ozone layer shields Earth from harmful UV radiation (skin cancer)
∴ Freeze CFCs at 1986 levels · ozone = UV shield
questions.ans: (i) In 1987 UNEP got countries to agree to freeze CFC production at 1986 levels (later, the Montreal Protocol phase-out). (ii) The ozone layer in the upper atmosphere shields the Earth's surface from harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation of the Sun, which causes skin cancer.
questions.remember: Ozone (O₃) high up: made by UV acting on O₂; shields us from UV. Ground-level ozone is a poison. CFCs from refrigerants and fire extinguishers deplete it.
questions.trap: Saying ozone blocks infrared radiation. It blocks ULTRAVIOLET.
questions.ncert: NCERT Ch 13 · Section 13.2.1 Ozone layer and how it is getting depleted
questions.tryit: Is ozone at ground level helpful?
questions.tryans: No, it is a deadly poison at ground level
